findings.message: Split successors get `seeded_by: rework-stage` on their `ticket_intake` signal. In merged code, `seeded_by` names the stem of the seeding ticket that owns those seeds. `merge.merge`, `MergeQueue._candidate`, and `stages._seeded_stems` select seeds by `seeded_by == stem`, then check them against `tickets/<stem>/checks.json` seed reviews. `rework-stage` is this ticket's own stem, so every Rework split successor would join the seed set of the stem `rework-stage`. Its seed-safety and re-run checks would then see foreign successors that have no seed review. The 'original-stem seed set unchanged' proof is false-green: it checks the wrong stem.
findings.paved_road: Drop `seeded_by` from split-successor `ticket_intake` bodies. The `supersedes` signal already records lineage, and no plan text asks for this metadata. Replace the criterion with a test that no `seeded_by` set changes for any stem after an update or a split.

findings.message: Split successors are stamped `source: seed`. The merged lint at `chupa/tickets.py:347` requires every `source: seed` ticket to cite `19.L` plus a `19.P<n>` unit under `## Plan contract`. It also refuses some sections. A split of a human-authored or box-authored original would produce successors that fail that lint, or would force invented plan citations. Rework split successors are not phase seeds.
findings.paved_road: Have split successors inherit the original ticket's `source`, as an update already does. State that criterion, and add a test that each successor passes `parse_ticket` against a non-seed original.

findings.message: An escalation's signal body is defined as `{signal: rework_escalate, rung: caps.next_rung(...)}`. `caps.next_rung` returns `None` once the ladder is exhausted (top model at `max` effort). Criterion 3 requires the body to carry a `rung`, and section 11.4 routes an exhausted ladder to the Reject queue. The ticket does not say what Rework emits in that case, and no test covers it.
findings.paved_road: Add a criterion: when `next_rung` returns `None`, Rework emits no `rework_escalate` signal and returns a typed Reject-queue routing result (an RMA). Name a test in `tests/test_rework.py` that pins this.
